evidence: The back-FFT consistency view built its round trip with DeltaPdfParams(crop_hkl=None) (src/nebula3d/server/consistency.py:137, and a band saved from it recorded the same, :202): the package defaults, whatever transform the run used, though the ΔPDF stage records its transform in the ΔPDF's provenance (transform_config, src/nebula3d/pipeline.py:1542, written at :1595). After a run with hann or another σ the view showed a round trip the run never made. No test compared the browser build's results with the native ones: tests/test_float32_equivalence.py compares float32 with float64, both in the low-memory mode its own webbridge.setup() call leaves on. And webbridge.setup() sets NEBULA3D_LOW_MEMORY=1 for the whole process (src/nebula3d/webbridge.py:209), which nothing unsets: tests/test_pooled_rings.py failed after tests/test_webbridge.py.
proposed_fix: The view, natively and in the browser (server.consistency.view_input), reads the run's window, σ, shape, support, padding and subtractions back from the ΔPDF's transform_config (pipeline.delta_pdf_settings_from_config), keeps the full |Q| range (crop_hkl stays None, by design) and the band applied in the view, and says where its settings came from in its response: settings.source is run, or defaults with a note saying why when the dataset has no readable record, and defaulted names what a partial record lacked. Its input is the volume the record says the ΔPDF was made from (source_file, reported as made_from), and the flattened volume, else the backfilled one, only when no record names one or that file is gone, as the note then says (settings.input and same_input show which). The reconstruction cache keys on the transform, and the page's header names the window and whose it is. A parity test runs one dev-split volume through the native engine and the browser bridge and pins which verdict-level outputs must be equal and which may differ, by the measured amount. An autouse fixture in tests/conftest.py puts the NEBULA3D_* environment back after each test and each module.
tests: tests/test_native_browser_parity.py (the stages' summaries, the ring decision, the punch, the ΔPDF, the back-FFT check and the consistency view; the ring test's thinner sampling in low-memory mode)
note: Approved by the manager on the user's delegation, 2026-10-19 (plan 4.12, the rest). Implemented in baaf115 and ca32b84 (the view, server and browser), c9209ac (the page's header), 8ff6c82 (the environment fixture) and dc05962 (the parity test). Arm A on dev re-run before and after: 32 of 32 entries identical, 5 of 8 cases pass, as recorded. The model-visible snapshots are unchanged: consistency_details reads the run's saved check, not the view. Measured on every dev case and the demo at 121³ and 161³, the browser's decisions are the native ones. Found, not tuned: the low-memory mode samples the ring test's shells more thinly (at most an eighth of the volume's voxels, src/nebula3d/preprocessing/ring_isotropy.py:290), so the browser measures the confirmed rings' signal-to-noise up to 2.6 times lower (on the 161³ demo, 7.0 against 3.8 at 6.94 Å⁻¹, where the rule asks 3): a ring near that threshold could be confirmed natively and left in the browser. Left: validation/score.py keeps its own reader of the same stamp (_params_from), which could take the new one.

decision.by: the manager, on the user's delegation
decision.option: the consistency view takes the run's settings; the browser build's verdicts pinned against the native ones
